tools.name: list_documents
tools.description:
List the user's documents. By default returns ACTIVE docs in their default workspace (their team workspace if they have one, personal otherwise). Use `which` to switch lens:
  • 'active'         — default. Docs the user owns or is a workspace member on. Has the user's own work.
  • 'trash'          — recently-trashed docs. Use when the user says "what did I delete" / "restore X" / "undelete".
  • 'shared-with-me' — docs OTHER people shared with this user (grants from other workspaces).

Returns slug, name, url, type, language, extension, owner attribution, and latest-version summary for each. Use this to find an existing doc's `slug` before calling `read_document`, a sharing or lifecycle tool, or an authoring tool.

tools.name: show_pdf
tools.description: DISPLAY a PDF to the user inline by slug — renders OFF your context (bytes go to the widget, nothing enters the conversation; returns metadata + an artifact reference, never the text). Use when the user asks to SEE a doc ("show / open / pull up X"). To load the TEXT into your context to summarize or revise, use `read_document` instead. `show_pdf` shows only a PDF; a wrong-type call names the right tool.

slug.description: The doc's 6-char slug (from `stash` / `list_documents` / URLs).

tools.name: show_page
tools.description: DISPLAY a web page to the user inline by slug — renders OFF your context (bytes go to the widget, nothing enters the conversation; returns metadata + an artifact reference, never the text). Use when the user asks to SEE a doc ("show / open / pull up X"). To load the TEXT into your context to summarize or revise, use `read_document` instead. `show_page` shows only a web page; a wrong-type call names the right tool.

slug.description: The doc's 6-char slug (from `stash` / `list_documents` / URLs).

tools.name: show_text
tools.description: DISPLAY a markdown / text / code doc to the user inline by slug — renders OFF your context (bytes go to the widget, nothing enters the conversation; returns metadata + an artifact reference, never the text). Use when the user asks to SEE a doc ("show / open / pull up X"). To load the TEXT into your context to summarize or revise, use `read_document` instead. `show_text` shows only a markdown / text / code doc; a wrong-type call names the right tool.

slug.description: The doc's 6-char slug (from `stash` / `list_documents` / URLs).

tools.name: read_document
tools.description:
Read a document's CONTENT into your context by slug — a SILENT read: NOTHING is rendered or shown to the user (no widget, no preview, no link card). This is the right FIRST call whenever you need the text to reason over — to summarize it, answer questions about it, or change it (then apply the change with the matching `edit_*` tool — edit_pdf / edit_page / edit_text — as surgical `{ old_string → new_string }` edits, same slug). Word and spreadsheet docs are view-only: read them, but they take no edits or new versions.

Returns the doc's metadata, a reference to its latest artifact (id, signed fileUrl, metadata), `content` — the full body text — for text-like kinds (html/md/text + agent-authored pdf print-HTML; binary files like an uploaded .pdf, .docx or .xlsx aren't text-extractable), and any unresolved lint `errors` on the latest version (this is ALSO the way to re-check errors mid-fix-loop — no separate errors tool).

Pass `withHistory: true` to also include the activity feed — every event newest-first (type, timestamp, author, and for content_pushed events the `artifactId` used by `revert_document`). To DISPLAY the doc to the user instead, call the matching `show_*` tool (show_pdf / show_page / show_text) — it renders inline entirely off your context.

A multi-page site (an older web page made of several files) has no single body: its files come back in `files` instead, read-only.

slug.description: The doc's 6-char slug (from `stash` / `list_documents` / URLs).

withHistory.description: If true, also include the activity history (event feed with artifact ids) in the response.

tools.name: screenshot_document
tools.description:
SCREENSHOT a staged document by slug — the rendered result comes back AS IMAGES for your own review, plus the deterministic `errors`. Renders the latest pushed version and returns:
  • `errors` — problems detected at render time. PDF: freeflow checks (content wider than the page can hold — an unbreakable string or too-wide table; a keep-whole block taller than one page; text buried under other text; a blank page mid-document; a broken image; a blank document). HTML: viewport + runtime checks (horizontal blowout on desktop or mobile, missing viewport meta, broken images, a blank render, uncaught boot exceptions, missing files, console errors). ALL advisory — nothing blocks a stash; fix them when iterating, never by stripping design.
  • screenshots delivered to YOU as image content — PDF: one image per page at `resolution` px wide (DEFAULT 500 — enough to judge layout / overflow / colour and cheap on tokens; raise to ~1000–1600 ONLY to read fine print), up to 8 pages per call. A bare call serves pages 1-8; pass `firstPage`/`lastPage` for a contiguous range, or `pages` for an EXPLICIT set like [2,5] so pages you did not touch never enter your context. When more pages remain than one call ships, the result names what shipped (`pageRange`) — call again for the rest. Everything else: a bounded full-height shot at DESKTOP and at MOBILE (390px) — so you can SEE the result and catch what the checks cannot: hidden text, wrong colours, a broken visual layout.

Call it after authoring or iterating a PDF or page to check your work BEFORE telling the user it is ready — especially when a create tool reported errors. The images return to YOU (the model); they are NOT the user-facing inline widget.

slug.description: The doc's 6-char slug (from a create_* result / list_documents / a docstash URL).

firstPage.description: PDF only, optional: 1-based first page of the range to screenshot — use when specific pages need review (the user says "pages 5-8 are broken") or to fetch the next window of a longer doc. Omit for the first 8 pages.

lastPage.description: PDF only, optional: 1-based last page of the explicit range (defaults to firstPage — a single page). At most 8 pages ship per call.

pages.description: PDF only, optional: EXPLICIT 1-based page numbers to screenshot, e.g. [2,5] — a discontiguous set. Use this after editing specific pages so untouched pages never enter your context. Overrides firstPage/lastPage. Max 8.

resolution.description: PDF only, optional: width in px of each page image. DEFAULT 500 — enough to judge layout, overflow, colour, and composition, and cheap on tokens (image cost scales with area, and these screenshots are your biggest token cost). Raise it (≈1000–1600) ONLY when you must read fine print. Prefer the smallest resolution that answers your question.

tools.name: list_org_members
tools.description:
List members of the user's default workspace: their names AND emails. Use this to figure out WHO TO SHARE WITH when the user says "share with the team" / "who's in this workspace?" / "share with Alice" (and you need to resolve Alice → email).

Returns nothing useful for a personal workspace (just the user themselves). For team workspaces returns the full member roster.

Use the emails returned here as the `email` argument to `set_access`.

tools.name: rename_document
tools.description: Change a doc's name. Metadata only: no new version is created. Use when the user says "rename X to Y".

slug.description: The doc's 6-char slug.

tools.name: set_trashed
tools.description: Move a doc to the trash (`trashed: true`) or restore it from the trash (`trashed: false`). Trash is RECOVERABLE: a trashed doc leaves the active list, appears in `list_documents` with which='trash', and comes back with `trashed: false`. Don't tell the user it's permanently gone.

slug.description: The doc's 6-char slug.

trashed.description: true = move to trash; false = restore from trash.

tools.name: revert_document
tools.description: Make an EARLIER version the doc's current version again. Get the version's `artifactId` from `read_document` with withHistory:true (each content_pushed event carries `payload.artifactId`). No content is lost: the revert is logged as a new event and the full history stays intact.

annotations.title: Revert document to an earlier version

slug.description: The doc's 6-char slug.

artifactId.description: The full id of the version to revert to (from `read_document` with withHistory:true).

tools.name: list_access
tools.description: List the people granted access to a doc (Viewers and Editors). Does NOT include public-link state: that's `document.isPublic` on `read_document`.

slug.description: The doc's 6-char slug.

tools.name: set_access
tools.description: Set one person's access to a doc: 'read' (Viewer), 'write' (Editor: can push new versions), or 'none' (remove their access). Also changes an existing Viewer to Editor or back. DocStash emails the person a link. They don't need an account: without one they can view the doc in their browser from that link, and they sign up to edit or download it. This is NOT a public link: only that person's link opens it. Resolve a name to an email with `list_org_members`. If the user didn't say whether the person may edit, ask before setting 'write'.

slug.description: The doc's 6-char slug.

tools.name: set_public_link
tools.description: PUBLISH a doc (`isPublic: true`) or unpublish it (`isPublic: false`). Published, anyone with the URL sees the latest saved version without signing in; this is the ONLY way to make a doc publicly viewable, and a stashed url stays private. The doc must be saved (stashed) before publishing. Unpublishing cuts off everyone using the public URL; people granted access and workspace members keep access. Returns the public docstash.ai `url` when published. Call only when the user explicitly asks to publish / make public / get a public or shareable link, or to unpublish.

slug.description: The doc's 6-char slug.

isPublic.description: true = publish (public link on); false = unpublish (public link off).

tools.name: create_pdf
tools.description: Generate a beautiful, print-ready PDF document for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW: reports, memos, proposals, letters, résumés, whitepapers, contracts, essays, one-pagers. THIS IS THE DEFAULT for a generic 'make me a document' / 'make me a PDF' request (use `create_text` for markdown/code source, `create_page` for a web page). `content` = HTML you author, and DocStash renders + presents it AS A PDF (paginated paper, page nav, zoom, one-click PDF download). Do NOT generate a binary .pdf; the user drag-and-drops pre-existing .pdf files on the dashboard. This is a REAL HTML/CSS document rendered by a full Chromium engine and baked to PDF — you have the SAME visual toolkit a web page has (any CSS layout, SVG, gradients, filters, transforms, web fonts, images), NOT a limited document format. It is a STATIC print document: NO `

name.description: Required when creating a new doc; omit when pushing a new version (use `slug` instead).

slug.description: Slug of an existing doc to iterate (from a create_* result, `list_documents`, or a docstash URL — a full URL is accepted). OMIT for a NEW doc; a stale slug OVERWRITES that doc. Iterate-vs-new rules: server instructions.

description.description: One-line commit-style changelog for THIS version (≤~8 words — the CHANGE, not the whole doc), e.g. "Add Q3 revenue table". Set it on every call; it becomes the version-history entry.

content.description: One continuous, top-to-bottom HTML document you author and design; DocStash flows it across US Letter pages and paginates for you. Build designed set-pieces (cover, dividers, full-page infographics) as `<section class="pdf-canvas">` — a FIXED one-page canvas where absolute positioning + full-bleed backgrounds are safe and content auto-fits the page — and let running text FLOW. `pdf-break` forces a page, `pdf-keep` keeps a block whole, `pdf-bleed` is a flowing full-bleed section; theme every page via `@page{background:…}`. Draw charts/graphics as inline SVG (static print doc — no JS). DocStash presents it as a real PDF.

tools.name: create_page
tools.description:
Generate a WEB PAGE (a single self-contained HTML file, rendered live) for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW: landing pages, visual/interactive dashboards, infographics, demos, interactive web apps and games (React, three.js, d3, … loaded from a CDN) — anything the user should SEE RENDERED rather than read as source. Content = a complete `<!doctype html>` document with everything inline (`<style>`, `<script>`) and any images/libraries referenced by absolute URL or CDN. IMAGES & FONTS — image/font URLs MUST be DIRECT files (a gallery/viewer page renders BROKEN); the direct-URL recipes, sizing, and custom-font rules are in the server instructions (VISUAL DOCUMENTS & MEDIA). Viewer provides chrome — don't wrap.
DocStash hosts it live. Load any JS deps as `<script type="module">` ESM (esm.sh) or inline them — never reference a local build-output path (the file won't exist).
ROUTING: a live page or web app → this tool, as ONE self-contained file (inline your CSS and JS). Markdown / source code / raw data → `create_text` (inert source, not a rendered page). A designed PDF document → `create_pdf`.

RESPONSIVE — the page MUST reflow + scroll on mobile: include the `<meta name="viewport">` tag and DON'T lock it to `height:100vh` + `overflow:hidden` (that traps phone scrolling). The viewer renders full-width, no extra scroll container.

Nothing is stashed yet — then STOP: do NOT call `stash` yourself; the user reviews the preview and saves it. Once stashed, the doc is at a PRIVATE url (the user, their workspace members, and people they've granted access) until published with `set_public_link`. Full lifecycle, slug/versioning, attribution + publish rules: DocStash server instructions.

slug.description: Slug of an existing doc to iterate (from a create_* result, `list_documents`, or a docstash URL — a full URL is accepted). OMIT for a NEW doc; a stale slug OVERWRITES that doc. Iterate-vs-new rules: server instructions.

description.description: One-line commit-style changelog for THIS version (≤~8 words — the CHANGE, not the whole doc), e.g. "Add Q3 revenue table". Set it on every call; it becomes the version-history entry.

content.description: A complete `<!doctype html>` document as a UTF-8 string, everything inline.

tools.name: create_text
tools.description:
Generate an INERT text artifact — markdown, source code, or raw data — for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW. This is for content the user READS AS SOURCE (typography for markdown, syntax highlighting for code), never executed or rendered as a page. Set `extension` to the file's extension, which the doc keeps for good (the extension is the file's kind and its download name):
  • 'md' — markdown. Content = the markdown source. For prose, notes, READMEs, technical docs, documentation of any kind.
  • any other extension — source code or data: 'py', 'ts', 'go', 'rs', 'json', 'yaml', 'csv', 'sql', 'vue', … Content = the raw source string. Omit `extension` for plain text (.txt).
A new version (`slug`) keeps the doc's extension: omit `extension`, or pass the same one.
ROUTING: scripts, code files, READMEs, configs, raw CSV/JSON → here. A LIVE rendered page → `create_page`. A designed PDF (and any generic 'make me a document/PDF' ask) → `create_pdf`.

Nothing is stashed yet — then STOP: do NOT call `stash` yourself; the user reviews the preview and saves it. Once stashed, the doc is at a PRIVATE url (the user, their workspace members, and people they've granted access) until published with `set_public_link`. Full lifecycle, slug/versioning, attribution + publish rules: DocStash server instructions.

name.description: Required when creating a new doc; omit when pushing a new version (use `slug` instead).

slug.description: Slug of an existing doc to iterate (from a create_* result, `list_documents`, or a docstash URL — a full URL is accepted). OMIT for a NEW doc; a stale slug OVERWRITES that doc. Iterate-vs-new rules: server instructions.

description.description: One-line commit-style changelog for THIS version (≤~8 words — the CHANGE, not the whole doc), e.g. "Add Q3 revenue table". Set it on every call; it becomes the version-history entry.

extension.description: The file's extension, no dot: 'md' for markdown, else the code or data file's ('py', 'json', 'csv', 'vue', …). Omit for plain text, or for a new version of an existing doc.

content.description: The content as a UTF-8 string: the markdown source, or the raw source / data.

tools.name: edit_pdf
tools.description:
The DEFAULT way to change a PDF — edit it in place, or copy it into a new one. Emit ONLY the changes as `{ old_string → new_string }` pairs, not the whole document. `edit_pdf` edits only a PDF; a wrong-type call names the right tool. When to edit vs re-run a create tool, and iterate-vs-new-doc: DocStash server instructions.

- `old_string` must be text that appears in the CURRENT source — call `read_document` first to get it, and copy it verbatim with enough surrounding context to match EXACTLY ONE place (or set `replaceAll`). Whitespace differences are tolerated. A stale or ambiguous `old_string` fails cleanly and changes NOTHING, so re-read and retry.
- `new_string` replaces it; an empty string deletes the matched text.
- Edits apply in order, each to the result of the previous.
- **In-place** (default): the change lands as a new version of `slug`, shown as a fresh inline preview.
- **Copy mode** (`copy: true` + `name`): leaves `slug` UNTOUCHED and produces a NEW doc — a filled-in copy with your edits applied. The TEMPLATE flow: keep one master, spin off variants (an invoice/offer-letter/report template → a copy per client). Returns the new doc's own slug.

slug.description: The 6-char slug of the SOURCE doc (from `stash` / `list_documents` / URLs). In-place: this doc gets a new version. Copy mode: the template read from — it stays untouched.

copy.description: If true, DON'T change `slug` — create a NEW doc that is a copy of it with the edits applied (the template flow). Requires `name`.

name.description: Name for the NEW doc when `copy: true` (ignored for an in-place edit).

old_string.description: EXACT text from the current source to replace — verbatim, with enough surrounding context to be unique. Whitespace differences are tolerated.

new_string.description: The replacement text. An empty string deletes the matched text.

replaceAll.description: Replace EVERY occurrence (default false — `old_string` must match exactly once).

edits.description: Ordered surgical edits; each applies to the result of the previous one.

description.description: Optional one-line summary of the change, recorded on the new version.

tools.name: stash
tools.description: STASH a preview (from a create_* tool) — the actual SAVE; the doc stays PRIVATE. The `slug` IS the doc's slug (creates it, or pushes a new version if the preview targeted an existing doc). ‼️ Do NOT call this automatically after a create_* call — a plain 'create X' request is satisfied by the preview alone. Call it ONLY when the user signals saving (save / stash / ship it / looks good) or clicks Stash in the inline preview; when in doubt, ask first. Returns the `url`. Stashing does NOT publish — to make it public, then call `set_public_link` with isPublic: true.

slug.description: The slug returned by a create_* tool.

name.description: Optional override for the doc name at save time (new docs only).

description.description: Optional one-line changelog OVERRIDE. Prefer setting this on the create_* tool instead — a changelog set here is lost if the user stashes the preview manually. Only use this to override the preview's stored changelog at save time.

tools.name: discard
tools.description: Discard a preview (from a create_* tool) without stashing it. Call this when the user rejects it (e.g. 'discard', 'never mind', 'don't save it'). The unsaved draft is moved to Trash (recoverable from there), so it can no longer be stashed unless restored.

slug.description: The slug returned by a create_* tool.

tools.name: get_organizations
tools.description: List the workspaces (personal + team; ids and tool names call them organizations) the user can save documents to, with the currently-active one flagged. Call this to resolve a spoken name like "my team workspace" to its id before set_organization. Call them workspaces when talking to the user.

tools.name: set_organization
tools.description: Switch the active workspace that NEW documents are created in, by organizationId (from get_organizations). Persists for this connection until changed. Existing documents remain reachable by slug regardless of the active workspace.

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Internal widget poll — the latest details for a preview (its current name + this version's status). Not for direct agent use.

slug.description: The slug returned by a preview tool.

artifactId.description: Internal — the artifact id the widget rendered, so status answers for THAT version (not the slug’s latest).

tools.name: get_file
tools.description: Internal — the inline preview widget fetches its own document bytes here. Not for direct agent use.

slug.description: The slug returned by a preview tool.

artifactId.description: Internal — the artifact id the widget rendered, so bytes are for THAT version.

link.description: Internal — return a signed storage link (fileUrl) the widget fetches itself, instead of inlined bytes.
